title: Labels come from NAB windows
note: Each series' known-cause failure windows come from NAB's combined_windows.json. Points inside a window are labelled True. These labels are used only in evaluate(), never in fitting or thresholding.

title: Causal window features
note: pandas .rolling() windows end at the current row and .shift() only looks back, so every feature at time t uses data ≤ t. A centered window would quietly use the future, which a live system can't do.

title: The five detectors
note: Statistical detectors compare x_t with statistics computed up to t-1 (note the shift(1)). Isolation Forest and LOF are fit on the probation period only, and LOF uses novelty=True so it can score unseen points. The ensemble converts each score to a percentile of its own probation distribution so detectors on different scales can be averaged.

title: Label-free thresholds
note: The alert threshold is a quantile of probation-period scores, so it is chosen without seeing a single failure. A refractory period (half a day) collapses bursts of consecutive alerts into one page, which is how on-call alerting works in practice.

title: Event-level evaluation
note: Operators care about failures caught, not points. A window counts as detected if any alert lands inside it; detection position measures how early (0 = start). Alerts outside every window are false alarms, normalized per week. PR-AUC is computed after probation for a threshold-free view.

title: Injection sandbox
note: Adds a synthetic anomaly (spike, level shift, drift, stuck sensor) sized in probation standard deviations, then re-runs every detector end-to-end. This is a quick way to learn each detector's blind spots: slow drift and flat-lines are much harder than spikes.
